description.value: A prospective longitudinal fMRI pilot study examined changes in effective connectivity among alcohol-related brain networks across the first year of college in late adolescents performing a go/no-go task.

spans.text: In this longitudinal functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) pilot study, we examined changes in neural responses to alcohol cues across the first year of college in a normative sample of late adolescents.

description.value: Participants were scanned three times during their first year of college: before classes, during the first semester, and during the second semester.

The following preprocessing steps were applied to the data: motion correction using FMRIB's Linear Image Registration Tool ( ); non-brain removal using FMRIB's Brain Extraction Tool ( ); high pass temporal filtering (performed separately for each half of the time series); spatial smoothing using a 6 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel; and grand-mean intensity normalization of the entire four-dimensional dataset by a single multiplicative factor.
